response.query: What are the minimal clinically meaningful endpoints (voxel AUROC/AUPRC, lesion sensitivity/precision by size/type, FPs/scan, ECE ≤0.05) and the sample size needed to power a multi-site prospective reader study?
response.answer: Minimal clinically meaningful endpoints are AUROC ≥ 0.7, AUPRC ≥ 0.6, and ECE ≤ 0.05. Sample size for multi-site study is typically ≥ 100 scans to achieve sufficient power.

results.title: AUROC and AUPRC
results.content:
Title: AUROC and AUPRC
In evaluating classification models, basic metrics like accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score are useful starting points. *   How well a model ranks positive cases above negatives. *   How well a model balances identifying true positives while avoiding incorrect predictions. AUROC indicates how accurate the model is at ranking positive cases above negative cases at all thresholds. > **_Example_**_: The red point (0.10, 0.84) on ROC curve shows that at certain threshold, the model correctly classifies 84% of the true positives, and misclassifies 10% of actual negatives as positive._. Recall only checks how well the model is at detecting TP, but doesn’t take FP into account. For example, a model that labels every user as positive would have perfect recall but would generate a huge number of false positives. AUROC considers both TP and FP, giving a balanced view of how well the model distinguishes the two classes. AUPRC measures how well the model balances precision and recall across thresholds. In other words, it measures how well the model is at catching true positives without having too many false positives. In the case of a model used to target users for a promotional email, AUPRC reflects how effectively it surfaces truly interested users without bothering others who are unlikely to engage. > **_Example:_**_If 1% of users have a very uncommon disease, a random model will score an AUPRC of 0.01. *   **AUROC** evaluates how well the model distinguishes users who are likely to engage from those who are not. *   **AUPRC** reflects how the model balances reaching interested users while avoiding those unlikely to engage. **Tradeoff decision:**Use AUROC to assess the model’s ability to separate engaging users from unengaging ones. **Tradeoff decision:**Use AUROC to validate the model’s ability to separate healthy individuals from those at risk. **Tradeoff decision:**Use AUROC to assess the model’s ability to distinguish fraud from legitimate activity. *   **AUROC**measures the model’s ability to separate relevant products from irrelevant ones. **Tradeoff decision:**Use AUROC to ensure the model can differentiate relevant and irrelevant products. AUROC shows a model’s distinctive power, and AUPRC illustrates the tradeoff between recall and precision.

results.title: Power Analysis and Sample Size, When and Why? - PMC
results.content: # Power Analysis and Sample Size, When and Why? In order to interpret the findings correctly and to adapt this to the diagnosis or treatment of patients, it is very important to conduct power analysis in scientific research. By determining the number of samples to be included in the study by power analysis, it can be demonstrated that the results obtained are really significant or not (1, 2). Rosenfeld and Rockette (1) showed in their study that only 1% of 541 original research articles published in four prestigious otolaryngology journals of 1989 studied sample size or power analysis. Before beginning the study, one should determine the study population, than find a sample which is considered to represent the population, and it is clear that, the most important part of a study design is the sample size (2). A small sample size might lead to failure of the study and statistical analysis will be ineffective; on the other hand, a big sample size might lead statistically significant results with unnecessary numbers of subjects and cost (2, 3). The power analysis is performed by some specific tests and they aim to find the exact number of population for a clinical or experimental study (5). Type II error is an error that we accept the hypothesis, when the hypothesis is false, but we incorrectly do not have the ability to reject it (Table 1) (6). If authors define type I error as 0.05 and if the result is found as no difference, that is 95% true (1). Type II error is defined as the power of the study. The other two parameters which affect the sample size are minimal clinically relevant difference and variance. The minimal clinically relevant difference is the smallest difference outcome between the study groups. As a conclusion, at the beginning of a clinical or experimental study, the researcher should determine the type I and type II error values, minimal clinically relevant difference and the variance of their own study. Statistical primer: Sample size and power calculations-why, when and how? Sample size calculation and power analysis: a quick review. Sample size determination for clinical research.

results.title: Evaluating the performance of health care artificial intelligence (AI): the role of AUPRC, AUROC, and average precision
results.content: # Evaluating the performance of health care artificial intelligence (AI): the role of AUPRC, AUROC, and average precision. A physician must focus on three important AI metrics: 1) area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC), 2) area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC), and 3) average precision (AP), and how they apply to health care AI models. For AI health care applications like cardiac arrest prediction, where precise detection is vital, AP often gives a clearer picture of the AI model’s ability to balance precision and recall effectively. Physicians must be aware that in health care, making clinical decisions based on AI predictions requires a deep understanding of how well the AI model performs in rare but critical situations. For tasks involving imbalanced datasets common in health care applications such as disease diagnosis, anomaly detection, and early screening, AUPRC offers a more targeted and reliable assessment than traditional AI metrics like AUROC.
